indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the `not runs` / `runs[0]` handling under the same guarded block (or add `isinstance(runs, list)`) so a non-list `workflow_runs` returns ('','') per the fail-soft contract.
evidence: Docstring at scripts/main_health_report.py:77-80 promises: 'Every failure mode ... or a malformed body — returns ("", "").'

ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_main_health_report.py parametrizes 'malformed body' ('not json'), 'unexpected shape' ('{"unexpected": true}'), and empty history, but never a body where workflow_runs is a non-list (e.g. a JSON object), so the uncaught-KeyError path is untested.
indeterminate.finding: resolve_last_green can raise an uncaught KeyError on a malformed-but-valid-JSON body, violating its documented fail-soft contract. `runs = payload["workflow_runs"]` is inside the try (KeyError caught), but `if not runs` and `newest = runs[0]` execute outside it; if the API returns `workflow_runs` as a truthy non-list JSON object, `runs[0]` raises KeyError and fails the report job.
scenarios: Actions API (or a proxy) returns a JSON object for workflow_runs instead of a list during a partial outage, on a red run when the responder most needs the report.
indeterminate.suggested_fix: After extracting `runs`, add `if not isinstance(runs, list): return "", ""` (or fold the list/index checks into the try/except that catches ValueError/KeyError/TypeError).

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat last_green_sha equal to head_sha as 'no distinct lower bound' (fall back to the placeholder or a flake note) rather than emitting a degenerate `git bisect start <sha> <sha>`.
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:153: `    if last_green_sha:` (accepts any non-empty value, including head_sha)

scripts/main_health_report.py:75: docstring: 'Return (sha, run_url) for the newest successful run of this workflow on branch' — on a flaky re-run of the same tip the newest success and the current head are the same SHA.
indeterminate.finding: The red-path bisect recipe does not guard against last_green_sha == head_sha, producing a degenerate `git bisect start <sha> <sha>` with an empty commit range.
scenarios: A flake reddens a scheduled run at the same main tip a prior scheduled run passed; the lookup returns that same SHA as the good bound.
indeterminate.suggested_fix: In _render_red, treat `last_green_sha and last_green_sha != head_sha` as the resolved-bound branch; otherwise use the NO_LOWER_BOUND path with a 'same SHA as HEAD — likely a flake' note.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] When the lower bound is unresolved, render the placeholder outside the runnable line (e.g. `git bisect start <bad> <GOOD>  # replace <GOOD>`) so the pasted command is not broken shell.
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:50: `NO_LOWER_BOUND = "<a commit you know was green>"`
tests/unit/test_main_health_report.py:114: asserts only the prefix `git bisect start badbad0000` is present, so a broken tail passes.
indeterminate.finding: When no lower bound resolves, the rendered 'copy-pasteable' bisect line becomes `git bisect start <bad> <a commit you know was green>`, whose `<`/`>` and spaces make it broken shell (looks like redirection plus extra args), contradicting the copy-paste framing.
scenarios: Missing-lower-bound degradation path (403, empty history, malformed body) renders the recipe with the placeholder substituted directly into the shell line.

indeterminate.finding: main()'s `--jobs` validation branches — `parser.error("--jobs must be valid JSON")` and `parser.error("--jobs must be a JSON object")` — are never exercised by any test, even though the workflow hand-authors the `--jobs` value as a multi-line JSON literal (JOB_RESULTS) that a future edit could break.
scenarios: A future edit to test.yml's JOB_RESULTS heredoc emits invalid JSON; the intended argparse error contract is never regression-covered.
